nodes.question: What perspective is proposed for understanding the governance of MSIs?
nodes.answer: A relational perspective is proposed for understanding the governance of MSIs, focusing on social processes and social relations.

In such a perspec- tive, MSIs are understood as an arena where heterogeneousactors meet. However, a common understanding about the governance of MSIs has not yet been established within interdisciplinary discourse (Bryson et al. 2015 ; de Bakker et al. 2019 ; Gazley 2017 ; Getha-Taylor et al. 2019 ; GI ckler 2020 ; van Tulder et al. 2016 ). The central question of this paper is therefore: how can the governance of an MSI inglobal economic relations be captured empirically to explain (un)achieved outcomes of the collaboration?Environmental Management (2025) 75:490 504 491 To answer this question, we propose a theoretical fra- mework for capturing and analyzing the governance of MSIs. We build this on work on the governance of inter- organizational (corporate) networks (GI ckler 2020 ; GI ckler and N meth 2012 ; Klijn et al. 2010 ; Provan and Kenis 2008 ). We understand the concept of networks from a relational perspective, which contributes to a better under- standing of social processes on the one hand and social relations on the other (Grabher 2006 ).

nodes.question: What are the three key elements of governance identified in the definition provided?
nodes.answer: The three key elements of governance are actors, processes, and structures.
nodes.paragraph: Three key elements of governance can be derived from this de nition: (a) actors, (b) processes, and (c) structures. The word use highlights the understanding of governance as a phenomenon that is constituted by the actions and interactions of actors (Bryson et al. 2015 ). Consequently, addressing these elements must go beyond rules on paper or institutional design (Bartley 2022 : 189). Accordingly, the literature on MSIs, collaboration governance, and net- work governance indicates negotiated (d) topics and out-comes as the fourth element (Clarke and MacDonald 2019 ; Edelenbos et al. 2010 ). In the following, the state of research on these four elements of network governance iselaborated in order to derive speci C sub-questions that, in accordance with the overarching research question, lead to the empirical measurement of governance thereby explain-ing (un)achieved outcomes of the collaboration.Actors Formally, all individuals and (parts of) organizationsinvolved in the MSI constitute the group of actors (Berardo et al. 2020 ). The question is, which actors are involved, and which are not?
